children: The additional acceptance period will run until 6 October, while Persistent is also preparing a funding plan of up to USD 1.25 billion for the acquisition

Persistent Systems has secured an 83.25 per cent stake in German IT services company Nagarro SE through its voluntary public takeover offer, paving the way for a planned delisting of the company from the Frankfurt Stock Exchange.

Galaxy Germany Holding SE, a wholly owned direct subsidiary of Persistent Systems, received tenders for 7,568,145 Nagarro shares during the offer’s acceptance period, which ended on 17 September 2026. The tendered shares represent approximately 61.15 per cent of Nagarro’s total share capital and voting rights, excluding treasury shares.

Persistent had previously secured a 22.10 per cent stake in Nagarro through a share purchase agreement with Lantano Beteiligungen GmbH. The combined holding has taken Persistent beyond the minimum acceptance threshold of 50 per cent plus one share required for the takeover offer to proceed.

Under the German Securities Acquisition and Takeover Act (WpÜG), Nagarro shareholders who have not yet tendered their shares can accept the offer during an additional acceptance period. The two-week window will run from 23 September to midnight CEST on 6 October 2026, at the same cash consideration of EUR 81 per Nagarro share.

Persistent will disclose the final number of shares tendered after the additional acceptance period ends. The company expects the transaction to close by the end of the first quarter of calendar year 2027, subject to a limited number of outstanding regulatory approvals.

Persistent Systems is also working on a funding plan of up to USD 1.25 billion as it prepares for the next stage of the proposed Nagarro acquisition, according to an earlier company update. The company has said it expects the combined business to maintain a mid-teen or higher growth profile over the next two to three years.

Persistent Systems Executive Director and CEO Sandeep Kalra said Nagarro’s growth is expected to improve gradually and converge with Persistent’s performance over time. He clarified that the mid-teen growth expectation is an aspiration and does not constitute formal forward-looking guidance.

Following the completion of the offer, Persistent intends to pursue the delisting of Nagarro shares from the regulated market, or Prime Standard, of the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, as soon as practicable and legally feasible. The company also intends to terminate trading of Nagarro shares on the open market of other stock exchanges.

The delisting from the regulated market would result in Nagarro’s exclusion from the SDAX and reduce the liquidity of its shares. Under the Business Combination Agreement, Nagarro’s Management Board is willing to support the delisting, subject to its fiduciary duties.

Sandeep Kalra, Chief Executive Officer and Executive Director, Persistent Systems, said the successful offer would allow the company to move towards combining Persistent and Nagarro and developing a global AI-led digital engineering business.
